title: Aphorism § 30
text:
§ 30  Sixth Edition



The human body appears to admit of being much more powerfully affected
          in its health by medicines (partly because we have the regulation of the dose in our own
          power) than by natural morbid stimuli - for natural diseases are cured and overcome by
          suitable medicines. 1


1  The short duration of the action of the artificial morbific
          forces, which we term medicines, makes it possible that, although they are stronger than
          the natural diseases, they can yet be much more easily overcome by the vital force than
          can the weaker natural diseases, which solely in consequence of the longer, generally
          lifelong, duration of their action (psora, syphilis, sycosis), can never be vanquished and
          extinguished by it alone, until the physician affects the vital force in a stronger manner
          by an agent that produces a disease very similar, but stronger to wit a homoeopathic
          medicine. The cures of diseases of many years' duration (§ 46), by the occurrence of
          smallpox and measles (both of which run a course of only a few weeks), are processes of a
          similar character.
